Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1125
Claimant:
Sarah Walters
Adjuster:
Jerry Hanson
5-25-24
First notice of loss was received for a side impact at an intersection, with the claimant reporting neck and back strain.
The claimant has retained counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.
6-7-24
Photos taken at the scene show damage that lines up with the described impact, and the vehicle damage is
consistent with a side collision. The file has no independent witness statements, so the photos carry most of the
weight at this stage.
7-26-24
Police report confirms the clamiant was in the vehicle at the time of the crash. The responding officer's notes match
the basic sequence of events given at intake.
8-19-24
The claimant's account of the collision has stayed the same in every conversation so far, including the initial call and
the recorded statement. No change in the description of how the crash happened has been noted.
8-25-24
Records search shows no earlier damage to the vehicle on file, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start
of coverage. The driver is a member of the policyholder's household and is covered as such.
9-16-24
Medical records were requested through counsel. No prior injury to the neck or back has been identified in the
claimant's history, and the reported strain is a plausible result of a crash of this type.
10-6-24
Treatment followed a typical course of care, with the claimant attending scheduled visits and progressing steadily.
The treating provider's notes show symptoms easing over the period of care.
12-6-24
Treatment has tapered as the claimant improved, and the most recent records show fewer visits and reduced
reported pain. Current status is being monitored against the medical file.
12-23-24
File reviewed. Vehicle damage, police confirmation of the claimant's presence, consistent accounts, and medical
course all align with the reported loss, and the claim remains open pending final medical documentation from
counsel.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
JSON format:
